subject: Post-call: SDK + Auth + Trace hook alignment for FastOps integration
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Peterson <liam@fastops.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: SDK + Auth + Trace hook alignment for FastOps integration

Thanks for your time this morning — quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned. Nice call, Liam.

Summary (from our discovery):
- FastOps will embed Redwood generation + embeddings for contextual assistant and a reranker for search results.
- Primary constraints: 20ms tail latency target for short prompts, 24/7 availability, and strict audit logging for customer data.
- Deployment: start on Redwood Hosted for PoC, with potential Dedicated pool later.

Technical asks we discussed (action items):
1) SDK & auth: We need a technical point-of-contact to test SDK init + API key rotation. Please confirm whether you prefer API keys or mTLS for the PoC.
2) Routing & model variants: We'll propose a routing policy to send latency-sensitive requests to smaller context models and fallback on higher-accuracy variants. Need your expected prompt length distribution.
3) Structured output & tool-calling: Share one representative schema for the assistant's structured responses (JSON schema or proto). We can map Redwood's function-calling layer to it.
4) Embeddings & reranker: Will you compute embeddings client-side or have us host an embeddings endpoint? If you host, we need the vector dim and distance metric.
5) Observability hooks (priority): We plan to surface X-Trace-ID propagation, X-Redwood-Latency headers, and include these logging fields: request_id, route, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit. Also propose a dashboard with per-route P50/P95/P99 latency and token-level cost.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Liam / FastOps: confirm API auth method + share sample prompt distribution (by EOD Thu)
- Connor (me as engineer lead): provide SDK quickstart snippet and a small test client (by Fri)
- Rachel: draft observability dashboard template and required logs/metrics (by Mon)
- I'll circulate a lightweight SOW and a checklist (attached) after you confirm auth approach.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf — includes SDK endpoints, header names (X-Trace-ID, X-Redwood-Latency), and a minimal audit-log schema.

Thanks — keen to get the PoC running next week.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198
From: Liam Peterson <liam@fastops.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: FastOps Engineering <eng@fastops.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK + Auth + Trace hook alignment for FastOps integration

Thanks Karthik — good summary. Quick replies inline: 

- Auth: for PoC let's do API keys (rotation via our secret manager). We may move to mTLS for Dedicated later.
- Prompt distribution: 70% short (<64 tokens), 25% medium (64-512), 5% long (>512). Most latency-sensitive flows are the short prompts.
- Embeddings: we'll host embeddings generation in our batch pipeline but would like a hosted embeddings endpoint from you for the initial reranker test. Vector dim is 1536 and cosine distance.
- Structured output: attaching a sample JSON schema for the assistant output (see Drive link).

Regarding observability, we can easily pass X-Trace-ID from our front-end. We'll want the latency header, and also the token count on responses if possible.

Attaching: fastops-arch-v2.png (network diagram) — will upload to the shared Drive.

Next: I'll confirm on rotation window for API keys by Fri. If you can share the SDK snippet, we'll run an initial smoke test next week.

-Liam
Lead Engineering Manager, FastOps
liam@fastops.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Peterson <liam@fastops.com>
Date: 2027-03-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: SDK + Auth + Trace hook alignment for FastOps integration

Connor / Rachel — forwarding the notes from FastOps. Highlights for you both:

- They will use API keys for PoC and want hosted embeddings endpoint for reranker test (1536, cosine).
- Prompt distribution skewed to short prompts — we should prioritize batching and low-latency kernels for small contexts.
- Observability: they will pass X-Trace-ID; they want X-Redwood-Latency + token_count returned.

Rachel: can you draft the dashboard template focusing on per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), token-level cost, and a trace sampling panel that links trace ids to request logs? Include a minimal query set for their ELK/Datadog.
Connor: please prepare a tiny SDK quickstart (Node + Python) that shows:
- init with API key
- sending X-Trace-ID header
- reading X-Redwood-Latency and token_count from response headers
- calling embeddings endpoint and reranker flow (simple example)

Also note SOW draft attached; I'll remove the legal boilerplate and send a slim PoC SOW to Liam after we confirm auth.

Thanks — pushing to get the smoke test by next Wed.

—
Karthik
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam Peterson <liam@fastops.com>
Date: 2027-03-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: SDK + Auth + Trace hook alignment for FastOps integration

Adding my notes and commitments:

What I'll deliver by Mon:
- Dashboard template (Grafana + Datadog snippets) with panels for per-route P50/P95/P99, tokens-per-request histogram, and a trace link field (clickable X-Trace-ID -> OpenSearch trace view).
- Log field spec: request_id, x_trace_id, route, model_variant, batch_size, token_count, kv_cache_hit, cost_usd. I'll include examples of JSON log lines and recommended indexing strategy.
- Alerting suggestions: P99 latency > 200ms for short prompts; sudden token_cost increase > 30% week-over-week.

Questions for FastOps (Liam):
1) Where will logs be shipped for PoC (our ingest or your ELK)?
2) Do you need pre-built Kibana/Grafana dashboards or just snapshot JSON to import?
3) Confirm retention policy for audit logs (how long should we preserve raw request/response for compliance?).

Connor — I'll coordinate on the sample queries you'll need to include in the SDK smoke tests (trace lookup by X-Trace-ID, token_count aggregation, per-model token cost).

Liam: if you can answer the three questions above, I'll finalize the dashboard and push it to the shared Drive.

—
Rachel Kim
Product Observability Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai
